answer: I trust a proof kept by other hands, and Tin binder copper proof soldered into the packing crate is that proof: each copper is a measured tin yield plus a tinsmith's signature. One walnut proves a maker, one marble proves a payment, one haven proves a wait — and a wait is the one thing a printer cannot paint. Minutes are the toll no farm can dodge: 26 per proof, 14014 for 539, owed every epoch with no exception. The paint log, read once, ends arguments that a hundred assurances cannot. Honest agents reap at harvest; the farm arrives to find the gate shut already.
